profile.summary: An endemic conifer shrub or small tree chiefly found in subalpine scrub and low alpine habitats, also occurring on low-elevation frost flats.
profile.lookFor: Flattened grey-green leaf-like stems, called phylloclades, with lobed or toothed margins; seeds develop on red fleshy scales.
profile.nameNote: NZPCN lists mountain toatoa; toatoa is shared with other celery pines. Its factsheet excludes the distinct unnamed yellow-foliaged P. aff. alpinus entity.

profile.summary: An endemic shrub or small tree of streamside forest and shrubland. Slender spreading branches carry rounded leaves that may be blotched brown or purple.
profile.lookFor: Opposite rounded leaves with fine hairs and a visible vein network; wide-angled twigs and red or sometimes white berries.

profile.summary: A widespread endemic rush forming clumps of erect wiry stems. It grows beside wetlands, in seasonally damp places and in open shrubland or pasture.
profile.lookFor: Smooth shining leafless stems with branching flower clusters appearing off to one side; species separation can require checking stem pith and capsules.
profile.nameNote: Wiwi is a shared rush name. NZPCN distinguishes this species from Juncus continuus and the Australian J. gregiflorus, with which it was formerly confused.

profile.summary: An endemic forest tree found from coastal areas to subalpine habitats. It can be common in disturbed forest and dominate some higher mountain forests.
profile.lookFor: Adult leaves usually simple with deeply toothed margins; white or pink flowers gather in narrow spike-like clusters.
profile.nameNote: The database spelling Weinmania racemosa is retained. Botanical references spell the former name Weinmannia racemosa; NZPCN now accepts Pterophylla racemosa and lists Weinmannia racemosa as its synonym. Tawhero is shared with other trees.

profile.summary: A bushy South Island shrub often found in upland stream valleys. It usually forms a rounded plant with short narrow leaves and white flower spikes.
profile.lookFor: Pairs of small glossy leaves widest toward the tip; white flower clusters and minute hairs on leaf margins and capsules.
